extractor.prompt: Extract founding relations and foundational structures in Derrida's Introduction to Husserl's Origin of Geometry, focusing on how higher-order objectivities (idealities) are constituted through founding acts and depend on pre-given strata.
extractor.note: Partial extraction covering section II (¶¶23-64) which develops the methodological foundations for Husserl's phenomenology of origin. Focuses on the doctrine of founding relations between proto-idealizations and perceptual ground, the necessity of pre-geometrical strata, the singularity of founding acts, and tradition as the medium of historical foundation. Not covered: sections III-VIII on specific Husserlian and Kantian developments.

coverage_note: Covers section II on methodological precautions and the doctrine of intentional history, particularly ¶¶27-28 (founded sense vs. factual rootedness), ¶¶40-48 (proto-idealizations and founding on perceptual substrate), ¶¶50-56 (founding acts and eidetic singularities), ¶57 (tradition as founding medium), and ¶63 (independence and dependence structure of ideal validity).

units.claim: Ideal geometric formations arise constitutively through proto-idealizations founded on the substrate of real, effectively perceived sensory experience.
units.quote: proto-idealizations on the substrate of a real, effectively perceived world

units.claim: The originary constitution of geometry necessarily presupposes and is founded upon a pre-geometrical stratum of sensory experience and practical measurement.
The singular founding acts that institute the sense of ideal objectivities are irreplaceable and foundational to all higher-order ideal signification.
units.quote: the singularities of origins are those of the founding acts of all ideal signification

units.claim: Tradition functions as the necessary constitutive medium through which founding acts are reactivated and ideal sense endures and circulates across time.
units.quote: tradition, as the ether of historical perception, then becomes necessary

units.claim: Higher-order objectivities possess normative validity independent of empirical historical transmission yet depend constitutively on founding intentional-historical acts.
units.quote: ideal validity is independent of factual transmission
